'''Huntington Faxon Willard''' (born c.1953) is an American [[geneticist]]. In 2014, he was named to head the [[Marine Biological Laboratory]], and is a professor in human genetics at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.capenews.net/falmouth/news/new-president-and-director-at-mbl/article_e38e0052-8476-11e4-a4b7-73f72c700f17.html|title=New President And Director At MBL|author=Enterprise Newspapers Staff|date=15 December 2014|work=CapeNews.net|accessdate=5 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mbl.edu/governance/gov_senior_staff/huntington-f-willard/ |title=Huntington F. Willard |accessdate=2015-04-02 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403132000/http://www.mbl.edu/governance/gov_senior_staff/huntington-f-willard/ |archivedate=2015-04-03 }}</ref>  He stepped down from leading the lab in 2017 to return to research.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mbl.edu/blog/huntington-f-willard-to-step-down-as-marine-biological-laboratory-president/|title=Huntington F. Willard to Step Down as Marine Biological Laboratory President|author=|date=|website=www.mbl.edu|accessdate=16 June 2017|archive-date=10 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180910131359/http://www.mbl.edu/blog/huntington-f-willard-to-step-down-as-marine-biological-laboratory-president/|url-status=dead}}</ref>  Willard was elected to the [[National Academy of Medicine]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.uchicago.edu/article/2016/10/17/mbl-director-huntington-willard-elected-national-academy-medicine|title=MBL Director Huntington Willard elected to National Academy of Medicine|author=|date=17 October 2016|website=uchicago.edu|accessdate=16 June 2017}}</ref>  Earlier, beginning in 2003 he was the Nanaline H. Duke Professor of Genome Sciences, the first director of the Institute for Genome Sciences and Policy, and Vice Chancellor for Genome Sciences at [[Duke University Medical Center]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]].

Willard graduated from the Belmont Hill School in [[Belmont, Massachusetts]] in 1971. He received his A.B. degree in [[biology]] from [[Harvard University]] in 1975 and his Ph.D. from [[Yale University]] in 1979. He did a postdoctoral fellowship in medical genetics at [[Johns Hopkins University]] from 1979-81.

He then held positions at the [[University of Toronto]] from 1982 to 1989, [[Stanford University]] from 1989 to 1992, and was Chairman of the Department of Genetics at [[Case Western Reserve University]] from 1992 to 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.genome.duke.edu/people/faculty/willard|title=GCB Faculty|author=|date=|work=duke.edu|accessdate=5 March 2016}}</ref>

His current research interests include [[genome]] sciences and their broad implications for medicine and society, human [[chromosome]] structure and function, [[X-inactivation]] and mechanisms of [[gene silencing]], and the first reported development of [[human artificial chromosome]]s for studies of [[gene transfer]] and functional genomics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dukehealth.org/AboutDuke/Administration/Administrators/MedicalCenter/HWillard|title=Huntington F. Willard, PhD at DukeHealth.org|website=dukehealth.org|accessdate=16 June 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20061207094225/http://www.dukehealth.org/AboutDuke/Administration/Administrators/MedicalCenter/HWillard|archivedate=7 December 2006}}</ref> Studies of the X-chromosome in his laboratory by [[Carolyn J. Brown]] led to the discovery of the human [[XIST]] gene, the [[Long non-coding RNA|long noncoding RNA]] associated with the [[X-inactivation|inactive X chromosome]].<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1038/349038a0|pmid=1985261|title=A gene from the region of the human X inactivation centre is expressed exclusively from the inactive X chromosome|journal=Nature|volume=349|issue=6304|pages=38–44|year=1991|last1=Brown|first1=Carolyn J.|last2=Ballabio|first2=Andrea|last3=Rupert|first3=James L.|last4=Lafreniere|first4=Ronald G.|last5=Grompe|first5=Markus|last6=Tonlorenzi|first6=Rossana|last7=Willard|first7=Huntington F.|bibcode=1991Natur.349...38B|s2cid=4332325}}</ref>
